headline: A one-team state that worships 1990s grit, buys for big families and dresses for the canyon, not the club.
thesis: The Jazz are the only major men's team for the whole Wasatch Front and beyond, from Ogden and Logan to Provo, St. George, southern Idaho and Wyoming. Volume is statewide, family-sized and kids-first, while taste is set by a thin layer: Sugar House and Granary District all-ages DIY culture, and the West Side's Pacific Islander and Latino hoop communities. Fans hold the Stockton-Malone-Sloan era as a moral standard and treat technical outdoor layers as everyday clothes. The gray-gradient City Edition repeats, and the Jazz are off the opening-night, Christmas and Specter stages, so this is a local year. Nike wins by turning the gray gradient into real Utah material (inversion haze, granite, salt crust) in cold-weather layers, building a Peterson-and-Bailey youth program sized for families, and using the year to earn West Side and DIY credibility ahead of a place-rooted 2027-28 City Edition.

archetype.name: The Statewide Family Loyalist
archetype.description: A fan who drives in on I-15 with three kids in youth jerseys, measures every new star against Stockton and Malone, and arrives in a puffer and beanie because the January walk to the Delta Center is cold. Loyal to the team over any brand, patient with a rebuild but allergic to hype.

pulse.teamMoment: Coming off 22-60, Utah speeds up its youth movement with No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey beside Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. Will Hardy is under pressure to develop them, and BetMGM's 35.5-win total asks for about 13 more wins.
pulse.sentiment: Impatient but curious: tired after a bottom-of-the-league year, energized by Peterson and the Jackson Jr. trade, and expecting visible progress and a play-in chase rather than a playoff run.

topInsights.title: The repeat City Edition needs a material story, not a relaunch
topInsights.insight: The vertical gray gradient with baby blue trim is on court for a second straight season, so there is no debut spike to sell. Every lens maps that gray onto something locals live with: the winter inversion haze, Wasatch granite, the salt crust of the Bonneville flats and a clear high-desert sky after a storm.
topInsights.implication: Refresh the gradient through textures and outerwear (salt-crackle print, granite-speckle fleece, inversion-to-sky fades) and never market it as new; save the big story for the 2027-28 City Edition.

topInsights.title: Buy for five kids, not one collector
topInsights.insight: Utah has the largest average household and the youngest median age of any state, and Jazz purchases are made in multiples on a once-a-season family trip to the Delta Center, a Murray or Orem mall, or Dick's. Deseret Industries thrifting and value-tier buying are normal, and authentic jerseys are a small collector niche.
topInsights.implication: Lead with deep youth and toddler sizing, matching kid-to-adult sets and bundle-friendly entry tees; keep premium to a small, clearly separated tier.

topInsights.title: Canyon wardrobe is game-night wardrobe
topInsights.insight: Locals ski Alta, Snowbird and Brighton after work, hoop in cold church and rec-center gyms all winter, and treat Black Diamond and Kuhl as status brands. Fleece, puffers, shells and beanies are what fans wear to the Delta Center from November through March.
topInsights.implication: Make outerwear and layering the core of the Jazz assortment, with ACG-adjacent fabrics and a ridgeline or strata detail, instead of summer-court streetwear.

topInsights.title: Two nostalgic eras, one untold origin
topInsights.insight: Fans divide into Note-era and 1996 Mountain-era loyalists, and both looks are thrifted at DI and cut up by younger fans. Almost nobody connects the purple, gold and green to the franchise's 1974 New Orleans Mardi Gras start and Pete Maravich.
topInsights.implication: Run separate era capsules rather than mixing palettes, and tell the New Orleans-to-Wasatch story as a credited Classic-style heritage line, all through team and NBA licensing.

topInsights.title: The West Side is the hoop engine and the least served
topInsights.insight: Rose Park, Glendale, West Valley and Kearns hold one of the highest per-capita Pacific Islander populations in the US plus large Latino communities, and they drive the valley's church-league, rec and high school basketball. They have few premium doors and appear on almost no Jazz product.
topInsights.implication: Co-create a capsule with paid, credited Tongan, Samoan and Latino designers through partners like PIK2AR, sell it in West Side doors, and send proceeds to local rec programs; never lift tatau, tapa or ceremonial patterns.

topInsights.title: Utah taste is all-ages and alcohol-light
topInsights.insight: Because of the state's liquor laws and young population, the scene grew up in all-ages rooms like Kilby Court, documented by SLUG Magazine in screen-printed flyer art. The local status object is a dirty-soda cup, not a pint glass.
topInsights.implication: Use gig-poster screen prints, cassette and 7-inch packaging and soda-shop color as the lifestyle graphic language, and keep beer and bar imagery off the line entirely.

topInsights.title: A calendar with local quiet zones and no national stage
topInsights.insight: General Conference empties the first weekends of April and October, many households keep Sunday as a family day, and Pioneer Day on July 24 is a bigger civic moment than any summer NBA date. The Jazz are on neither the opening-night nor the Christmas slate.
topInsights.implication: Stage in-person drops on Fridays and Saturdays around home Cup Nights, push Sunday demand to digital, and plan December as local family gifting rather than a national TV moment.

collection.name: Wasatch Front
collection.story: A collection built from the strip of land every Jazz fan shares: snow and granite above, salt and lake below, and gyms, all-ages rooms and family courts in between. It makes the gray City Edition feel like Utah, honors the two eras fans already love, and hands the West Side and DIY scenes the pen.

uniform.narrative: The state's namesake lake is shrinking, and Utahns feel it: the salt crust, the pink north arm and the shoreline contours are shared civic icons and a live civic worry. A salt-white City Edition with shoreline contour lines and land-speed numerals from the Bonneville salt flats tells a story only Utah can wear, and pairs it with a real conservation commitment. It moves decisively away from the two-season gray gradient while keeping the franchise's purple as its anchor.
motifs: Tonal shoreline contour lines across the body, drawn from Great Salt Lake topography rather than any artwork
Salt-crust crackle texture in the side panels
Hand-painted land-speed numerals and pinstriping from Bonneville Speed Week culture
A single Wasatch ridgeline at the hem, the mountains seen from the lake
uniform.typography: Custom numerals in the style of hand-painted land-speed race numbers, shale with a thin purple pinstripe outline; a clean sans wordmark with grid-coordinate styling.
details: Jock tag set in Salt Lake grid-coordinate typography, the way locals give directions
Waistband tape with a salt-crust print fading to north-arm pink
Neck tape carrying a single ridgeline-to-shoreline line
Court tie-in: a salt-white baseline band with pink shoreline contours
Hangtag and launch tied to a recognized Great Salt Lake conservation partner with a donation per jersey
avoid: Repeating the vertical gray gradient or baby-blue trim as the lead story
Replicating Spiral Jetty or any Smithson-derived spiral without Holt-Smithson Foundation engagement
Temple, Temple Square, pioneer-trek or any Latter-day Saint sacred imagery, and Pacific Islander or Native ceremonial patterns
Utah red, BYU blue or Utah State navy, Olympic marks and Utah Mammoth cues that blur team identity
Treating the lake as pure decoration without a conservation partner

partners.idea: Co-lead designer recruitment and cultural review for the West Side Court Collective, with paid roles and proceeds to youth rec.

partners.name: Salt Lake Arts Council (Living Traditions Festival)
partners.why: Runs Living Traditions and public-art programs that reach Pacific Islander, Latino and other community artists.
partners.idea: Host the May reveal of the West Side capsule at Living Traditions, with the artists on site.

partners.name: Craft Lake City
partners.why: Runs the state's busiest maker marketplace and can introduce vetted screen printers and designers.
partners.idea: Curate the monthly Delta Night poster artists and printers, and use DIY Fest to scout the next season.

partners.name: Kilby Court
partners.why: The emotional center of Utah's all-ages DIY scene and where young taste is set.
partners.idea: Sell each month's poster tee at a Kilby show the week of release, with the poster artist doing the night's flyer.

partners.name: SLUG Magazine
partners.why: Has documented Salt Lake Under Ground for decades; its poster culture is the graphic reference.
partners.idea: Editorial partner for the poster series: artist profiles and a printed season-set zine.

partners.name: Kuhl
partners.type: Salt Lake City outdoor apparel brand
partners.why: A hometown outdoor brand with real local cachet in a market where outdoor fluency is status.
partners.idea: Explore a co-branded Inversion Layer shell under a partner agreement, sold in both brands' doors.

partners.name: Utah Pride Center
partners.why: Runs Utah's Pride programming and is the right partner for authentic queer engagement.
partners.idea: Commission a queer Utah artist for a June piece with proceeds to the Center, not a logo swap.

partners.why: Recognized Salt Lake artists whose mural and graphic work could carry a credited limited release (outreach pending).

risks.risk: Palette confusion: the dossiers treat navy and yellow as the current identity, but the repository's own team record lists purple, black and white, so youth and core product could ship in the wrong colors.
risks.mitigation: Confirm the 2026-27 Association, Icon and Statement palette with the team before any colorway is locked; the City Edition and heritage lanes are unaffected.

risks.risk: City Edition fatigue in a second season of the same gray gradient.
risks.mitigation: Sell it as material and outerwear, never as new, and announce the 2027-28 direction early.

risks.risk: Cultural missteps with Pacific Islander, Latino, Native or Latter-day Saint imagery in a state that watches closely.
risks.mitigation: Co-create only through paid, credited partners such as PIK2AR and the Salt Lake Arts Council, keep all church and temple imagery out, and run cultural review before sampling.

risks.risk: Licensing gaps on Note and Mountain marks, Stockton, Malone and Sloan likenesses, local food brands and Smithson-derived imagery.
risks.mitigation: Clear team, NBA, player and estate rights first, and use unbranded cues (soda-shop color, salt texture) where licensing is uncertain.

risks.risk: Rebuild volatility: a slow start or deadline move can swing demand between Peterson, Bailey, Markkanen and Jackson Jr.
risks.mitigation: Hold player-specific depth on youth tees and fast-print capacity, and re-weight after the first month and at the Feb 11 deadline.

scorecard.rationale: A small metro but a whole-state, family-sized, youth-heavy buyer base with deep one-team loyalty and an unusually distinct design vocabulary (salt, snow, all-ages DIY, West Side hoops). Retail is dispersed along I-15 with a thin boutique layer, and a rebuild year with no national stage caps the near-term upside.
